statement.p: How many permutations of {\left\{1,2,3,4,5,6\right\}} leave exactly 1 element fixed?

solution.p: First pick one of the 6 elements to be fixed. For each such choice, derange the remaining 5, using the standard advanced PIE formula. We get {6 \choose 1}\left( 5! - \left[{5 \choose 1}4! - {5 \choose 2}3! + \dots {5 \choose 5}0! \right] \right) permutations.
